title: Everest Helicopter Tour: Weather, Landings and Prices
meta_description: Everest heli tour guide: morning flight plan, weather and payload limits, 10–15 minute landings above 5,000 m, who should not fly, shared vs private prices.
summary: An Everest helicopter tour flies from Kathmandu to Lukla, up the Khumbu to circle base camp, lands on the Kala Patthar ridge for 10–15 minutes when rules and weather allow, and stops for breakfast at Hotel Everest View. It takes 4–5 hours. Shared seats cost from about US$1,100–1,400; a private charter about US$5,000–6,500.

sections.heading: How the morning runs
paras: Every Everest heli tour is a morning trip, because cloud usually builds over the Khumbu from late morning. We collect you from your Kathmandu hotel at about 5:45 am, and after a weigh-in and safety briefing at the domestic terminal the helicopter takes off at around 6:30 am. It flies east for 45–50 minutes, with Langtang, Gauri Shankar and Numbur on the left, and lands at Lukla to refuel.

From Lukla the helicopter follows the Dudh Koshi past Namche Bazaar and Tengboche, then the Imja and Khumbu valleys over Pangboche, Dingboche and Lobuche. It circles above Everest Base Camp and the Khumbu Icefall and, when permitted, lands on the Kala Patthar ridge at about 5,550 m, facing Everest, Nuptse and Lhotse. The return stops at Hotel Everest View at 3,880 m for breakfast on the terrace, then flies back via Lukla, landing in Kathmandu between 10:30 am and noon.

sections.heading: Weather and the best months
paras: Helicopters in the Khumbu fly by sight, not by instruments, so the pilot needs clear air at Lukla, in the valleys and at the landing point. On a typical good day the sky is clear at dawn, cloud forms over the lower valleys by 9 or 10 am and the high peaks disappear by noon. That is why the tour leaves at first light and why delays are measured in hours, not minutes.

The steadiest months are October to December and March to April. January and February are often perfectly clear but very cold, with strong winds at altitude on some days. Late May brings haze and earlier cloud, and from June to August the monsoon makes most flights uncertain. If the morning is not flyable, we wait for a gap or move the tour to the next clear morning, so keep a spare day in Kathmandu after the planned date.

sections.heading: Payload: why groups sometimes split
paras: The helicopters used in the Khumbu, mostly the Airbus AS350 B3 and H125, carry a pilot and up to five passengers at Kathmandu's altitude. Thin air reduces lift, so at 5,000 m and above the same aircraft can safely carry only two to three passengers, depending on temperature, fuel and body weight.

Operators handle this in two ways. Some drop two passengers and spare fuel at Lukla or Pheriche, take the first group to Kala Patthar, then return for the second group. Others land everyone at Hotel Everest View first and shuttle in pairs. Either way, the total time on the ground at the high point stays short, and passengers are weighed before departure. Hand luggage is usually limited to about 10 kg per person, so leave large bags at your hotel.

sections.heading: Landing rules and time on the ground
paras: Landing points are the part of the tour most likely to change, so we treat them as a plan, not a promise. As we understand it, tourist helicopters are generally not allowed to land at Everest Base Camp itself except for rescue, and permission to land on Kala Patthar has been granted at some times and withdrawn at others. The local municipality has also announced limits on tourist flights in recent years, with uneven enforcement. Check current status before you travel.

When a high landing is possible, the time allowed on the ground above 5,000 m is usually 10–15 minutes. That is deliberate: arriving from 1,400 m in under two hours gives your body no chance to adjust, and even fit people can feel dizzy, breathless or nauseous within minutes. If a high landing is not allowed or not safe that day, the pilot flies over base camp and lands at a lower point such as Hotel Everest View.
list: Walk slowly after landing and do not run for photographs
Drink water on the flight and avoid alcohol the night before
Tell the crew straight away if you feel faint, confused or very short of breath
Use the onboard oxygen if offered; it is there for this reason

sections.heading: Who should not fly to high altitude
paras: A heli tour suits most healthy adults, including grandparents who could never trek to base camp. It is not suitable for everyone at the high landing. We ask anyone in these groups to speak to a doctor first and, in most cases, to stay in the helicopter or wait at Hotel Everest View while the others land higher.
list: People with heart disease, a history of heart attack or uncontrolled high blood pressure
People with lung conditions such as COPD or severe asthma
Infants and very young children, who cannot tell you how they feel
Anyone with a recent operation, a recent serious illness, sickle cell disease or severe anaemia
Anyone who has had a cold or chest infection in the past week

sections.heading: Heli tour or trek: which suits you
paras: A heli tour and a trek show the same mountains in very different ways. The tour gives you Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse and Ama Dablam at close range in one morning, without any training, acclimatisation or nights in cold lodges. It suits travellers short of time, families with older members, people who have trekked before and want to return, and photographers who want an aerial view of the Khumbu Glacier.

What it cannot give you is the Khumbu itself: the Sherpa villages, monasteries, lodges and the slow change from pine forest to glacier that makes the trek worthwhile for many people. Some travellers combine the two, walking the 7-day Everest View trek to Namche and Tengboche and flying out, or trekking to base camp and taking a helicopter back from Gorak Shep. We can build either into an itinerary, and the heli section is always subject to the same weather and payload rules.

sections.heading: Shared seat or private charter: prices
paras: A shared seat means you fly with up to four other travellers, usually strangers, on a fixed plan. Our shared-seat tour costs from ₹1,05,000 or US$1,190 per person, which sits within the usual market range of about US$1,100–1,400. The operator sells seats until the helicopter is full, so a departure may wait for enough bookings, and the route and stops are fixed.

A private charter books the whole helicopter for your group of up to five, at roughly US$5,000–6,500 per helicopter. That works out at US$1,000–1,300 per head for five people, close to the shared price, and it buys flexibility: your own departure time, the choice of a longer stop at Hotel Everest View, and the option of a family member staying lower without disrupting strangers. For three people or fewer, shared seats are better value.

faqs.q: How much does an Everest helicopter tour cost?
faqs.a: A shared seat on our Everest heli tour from Kathmandu costs from ₹1,05,000 or US$1,190 per person, including the Kala Patthar landing when permitted and breakfast at Hotel Everest View. A private charter for up to five passengers costs roughly US$5,000–6,500 per helicopter. Prices depend on fuel costs and the season.

faqs.q: Can I do the Everest heli tour with kids or elderly parents?
faqs.a: Older children and healthy older adults usually manage the tour well, since there is no walking. Infants and very young children should not land above 5,000 m, and anyone with heart or lung disease should ask a doctor first. Those who should not go high can stay in the helicopter or wait at Hotel Everest View at 3,880 m.

faqs.q: Does the helicopter land at Everest Base Camp?
faqs.a: Generally not. As we understand the current rules, tourist helicopters do not land at base camp itself except for rescue; tours circle above it and land on the Kala Patthar ridge when permitted, which gives a better view of Everest's summit anyway. Landing rules have changed several times, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long do you stay at Kala Patthar on a heli tour?
faqs.a: Usually 10–15 minutes. You arrive at about 5,550 m less than two hours after leaving Kathmandu at 1,400 m, without any acclimatisation, so staying longer raises the risk of altitude sickness. It is enough time for photographs of Everest, Nuptse and Lhotse. The longer stop is breakfast at Hotel Everest View, about 45 minutes.

faqs.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day?
faqs.a: The helicopter flies only in clear visual weather. If the morning is cloudy, the operator may wait an hour or two for a gap, or move the tour to the next clear morning. If the weather turns while you are in the Khumbu, the pilot may shorten the route or skip the high landing. Keep a spare day in Kathmandu.

faqs.q: Is a private helicopter charter worth it?
faqs.a: For groups of four or five, often yes. A private charter costs roughly US$5,000–6,500 for the helicopter, about the same per head as shared seats, and lets you choose the timing, stay longer at breakfast and adjust the plan if someone feels unwell. For one to three people, shared seats are usually much better value.

faqs.q: What should I wear on an Everest helicopter tour?
faqs.a: Dress for −10 °C at the landing even on a warm Kathmandu morning: a down jacket, warm hat, gloves and sunglasses, with comfortable shoes that grip on rock and snow. Wind on the Kala Patthar ridge makes it feel colder. Bring a small bag only; most operators limit hand luggage to about 10 kg per person.

faqs.q: Will I get altitude sickness on a heli tour?
faqs.a: Mild symptoms such as light-headedness, a headache or breathlessness are common at the high landing, but serious illness is unlikely because you spend only 10–15 minutes there. Move slowly, avoid alcohol the night before and tell the crew if you feel unwell. Symptoms usually ease as soon as the helicopter descends to Hotel Everest View.

faqs.q: Which months are best for an Everest helicopter tour?
faqs.a: October to December and March to April have the most reliable morning weather. January and February are often clear but cold and occasionally windy. Late May is hazier, and June to August, the monsoon months, bring frequent cloud and cancelled flights. In any month, the earliest departure gives the best chance of clear views.
